objective: By the end you can walk a material chain across the four people: the request, the quotes, the order, the delivery checked at the gate (a short load, torn bags returned), the stock, the supplier's bill checked against the order and the delivery, and the payment; and the month-end stock count.

scenes.title: Cement runs short
beats: Tuesday, seven in the morning. At the Main block, six people are on site, and there is no cement.
The masons can lay nothing, plaster nothing. They will be paid for the day all the same.
Ravi asked for a hundred bags last night. Between his message and a mason mixing mortar there are four people, three suppliers, a lorry, two papers and a bill. This episode follows every one.

lines.text: Request → quotes → order → lorry → bill → payment

scenes.title: One chain, three papers that must agree
beats: Every material a site uses comes down the same chain.
The site asks. The office gets prices, and orders from the best. The order says what, how much, at what rate, and when.
The lorry comes with a challan: what was sent. At the gate, someone counts what actually came, and what was fit to use.
The bill comes later. Before a rupee is paid, three papers must agree: the order, the challan as counted at the gate, and the bill.
Where they do not agree, the difference is money: a short load, a torn bag, a rate that crept up. Checked, it is caught. Not checked, it is simply paid.

scenes.title: Who does what
beats: Who does what?
Ravi asks for the cement, and counts it at the gate.
Anil decides how much and from whom, and places the order.
Meera checks the bill against the order and the gate, and pays.
And the supplier, Malabar, sends the lorry, the challan and the bill. Ramesh sees what is owed, and at the month's end signs off what the count found.

scenes.eyebrow: In Mesiri · Requests, Stock · Tuesday 8 am
scenes.title: First, get the masons working
beats: Tuesday, eight o'clock. Ravi's request is the first thing on Anil's screen: a hundred bags for the Main block, with why.
Ordering takes days. But Stock shows the Annex holding a hundred bags, and the Annex uses only ten a day for its plinth beam.
So Anil moves forty bags from the Annex to the Main block, today. A tractor trip across the site, and the masons work by ten.
The move is a record too: the Annex's count goes down, the Main block's goes up, and nothing is lost between them.

scenes.title: Three suppliers, the same list
beats: Then the order itself. Cement for the next weeks, and steel for the Main block's staircase: two hundred bags and a thousand kilos. Anil asks three suppliers for a price on the same list.
Malabar comes back with cement at four hundred rupees a bag, the cheapest of the three. But its steel is seventy-two rupees a kilo.
Kerala Steels: cement at four hundred and twelve, steel at sixty-six. Sri Hardwares sits in the middle on both. Same list, three answers. Which is cheapest depends on what you compare.

scenes.title: Cheapest per item, or cheapest in total?
beats: In Mesiri, Anil sends the request to the three from Quotations, and their rates go in as they come.
The compare shows what the eye misses. Cheapest cement: Malabar. Cheapest in total: Kerala Steels, at one lakh forty-eight thousand four hundred.
And cheaper than both: split it. Cement from Malabar, steel from Kerala. One lakh forty-six thousand. Two thousand four hundred saved by reading one table.
Anil orders the split: two hundred bags of cement from Malabar at four hundred, two days to deliver, and the steel from Kerala Steels at sixty-six.

scenes.title: What the lorry says it brought
beats: Friday, the lorry. The driver hands Ravi the challan: two hundred ordered, a hundred and ninety sent. Ten to follow.
Ravi counts at the gate, as he should. A hundred and ninety bags, yes. But six are torn and set hard. He refuses them, there and then, with the driver watching.

scenes.title: Counted at the gate, said at the gate
beats: Ravi puts in what came, against the order, from the website: a hundred and ninety bags on the challan, six of them torn and set hard.
Mesiri ties it to Anil's order. The order now shows a hundred and ninety received, and ten still to come.
The six torn bags go back on a return note, a credit Malabar owes Green Villa. Nobody has to remember it at the month's end.

scenes.title: Six bags, two thousand four hundred rupees
beats: This is the return note that goes back with the lorry: six bags, torn and set hard, two thousand four hundred rupees.
In Mesiri it is a return against Malabar the same day, with a debit note: what the company owes Malabar drops by two thousand four hundred, before their bill even arrives.

scenes.title: The bill: one line, two problems
beats: Monday, Malabar's bill, dated Sunday. One line: a hundred and ninety bags of cement, at four hundred and ten.
Two problems in one line. The rate: the order said four hundred. And the quantity: a hundred and ninety, when a hundred and eighty-four were good and six went back.
Ten rupees a bag is easy to miss on a bill of a lakh. That is why nobody should have to spot it.

scenes.title: The bill, checked against the order and the gate
beats: Meera puts the bill in under Malabar, against Friday's delivery, exactly as it came.

Mesiri lays it beside the order and the gate: ordered at four hundred, billed at four hundred and ten. A hundred and ninety billed, six of them sent back. The difference, in rupees, before anything is paid.

Meera takes that bill back and asks Malabar for a corrected one. It comes the next day: a hundred and eighty-four bags at four hundred, seventy-three thousand six hundred. The return is settled against it, and that is what she pays on Saturday.
The money that leaks in most companies, a few rupees a bag, a few bags a load, stays here.

scenes.title: Back above the line
beats: And on site, the cement is back. The Main block holds a hundred and eighty-eight bags: what the gate kept, less what has been used since. Twenty-five days at this week's use.
Ten bags are still to come on Malabar's order. Anil does not chase them from memory: the order shows them as not yet delivered, until they are.

scenes.eyebrow: In Mesiri · Stock count · Monday 30 Nov
scenes.title: What is really there
beats: The last day of November. Ravi counts the Main block's store, bag by bag, and puts in what he finds, on Stock count.
Mesiri puts it beside the book: what came, minus what was used, minus what went back. Three bags fewer than the book.
Ravi says why: wastage, spilt and set on the mixing floor. A small, honest difference, and now it is written down.

scenes.eyebrow: What the owner sees · Monday · day 16
scenes.title: Paying for what came
beats: What does Ramesh see of all this? Two screens.
Malabar, on Suppliers: the bill that was taken back, the corrected one for what was kept, the six bags sent back, and what is owed now. He did not have to ask anyone.
And the month's count: three bags short at the Main block, wastage, one thousand two hundred and twenty-eight rupees, at what the bags cost. He approves it, and the book is the store again.
Three leaks this month, each caught by the person whose step it was: at the gate, at the bill, and at the count.

scenes.title: Six ways a load of cement leaks money
beats: Six ways a load of cement leaks money.
A crew standing idle while the order is placed. Two days of six people is twelve days' wages for nothing.
Ordering from one supplier without asking three, or comparing the wrong total.
A short load signed for at the gate, or torn bags accepted because the driver was in a hurry.

And a bill paid as it comes: ten rupees a bag above the order, six bags that never stayed. Small on one bill, a margin across a year. And a store never counted: nobody knows what is missing until the job is over.

scenes.title: Three questions
beats: Three questions. Pause, and answer them before you go on.
One: the Main block has no cement, and an order takes days. What does Anil do first? Move bags from a site that has them, the same morning.
Two: which three papers must agree before Meera pays? The order, the challan as counted at the gate, and the bill.
Three: Malabar's bill says a hundred and ninety bags at four hundred and ten. What is wrong? The rate, against the order's four hundred, and the quantity, against the hundred and eighty-four kept.
Next: wages week. The attendance Ravi sends every morning becomes Saturday's wage sheet. Now play the material chain yourself: chapters five and eight of the guided project.
